sub_theme: Settling into Year 2 / My New Class

lessons.title: Welcome Back: Sharing Our Summer
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to participate in a discussion, listening and responding to others.
success_criteria: I can share something about my summer.
I can listen to a friend and ask a question.
lessons.starter_activity: Circle time: quick round of one word to describe the summer.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model good discussion skills — listening, responding, asking a follow-up question.
lessons.independent_task: In pairs, children share a summer highlight and ask each other a question, then feed back one thing about their partner.
key_questions: What did you do this summer?
What question could you ask your partner?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note discussion and questioning skills as a Year 2 baseline — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Share one interesting thing learned about a classmate.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family what you're looking forward to in Year 2.

lessons.title: Counting to 100 (Recap and Extend)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count forwards and backwards within 100.
success_criteria: I can count forwards to 100.
I can count backwards from 100.
lessons.starter_activity: Count around the class as far as possible.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting forwards and backwards within 100 using a 100 square.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise counting forwards/backwards from different starting points using a 100 square.
key_questions: What comes after 49?
What comes before 60?
lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline check of counting range moving into Year 2 — evidence for MATHS.N1.

lessons.title: How I've Grown Since Reception
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how they have changed and grown since they were younger.
success_criteria: I can describe one way I've grown.
I can compare myself now to when I was younger.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a photo from an earlier year if available.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how children grow and change (height, skills, independence).
lessons.independent_task: Children record one way they've grown/changed since starting school.
key_questions: What could you not do before that you can do now?
How have you grown?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of growth and change, building towards animal offspring learning later this term — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Share growth examples with the class.
lessons.home_link: Look at an old photo of yourself with your family.

lessons.title: My Year 2 Self-Portrait
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to draw a self-portrait with increasing accuracy and detail.
success_criteria: I can draw my face with correct proportion.
I can add detail (freckles, glasses, hairstyle).
lessons.starter_activity: Look in mirrors and discuss facial proportion.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Recap proportion from Year 1, modelling more detailed observational drawing.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw a detailed self-portrait, comparing to their Year 1 one if available.
key_questions: What detail can you add this year that you couldn't before?
Where do your eyes sit on your face?

differentiation.support: Use a simple guide for proportion
differentiation.greater_depth: Add fine detail and shading independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Compare to Year 1 self-portrait to show progress — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.plenary: Display portraits and discuss progress since Year 1.
lessons.home_link: Draw a family member's portrait together.

lessons.title: Story Time: Starting Year 2
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to make a prediction and check it against the story.
success_criteria: I can make a prediction.
I can say if I was right.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at the front cover and predict the story.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a story about starting a new school year, pausing to check predictions.
lessons.independent_task: Children record their prediction and whether it came true, with reasoning.
resources_needed: Story book about a new school year
key_questions: What do you think will happen next?
Were you right?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note prediction skill, a Year 2 comprehension objective — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Predict what might happen next in a book you're reading.

lessons.title: Tens and Ones to 100
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent numbers to 100 using tens and ones.
success_criteria: I can show a number using tens and ones.
I can say how many tens and ones make a number to 100.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap tens and ones to 30 from Year 1.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model representing numbers to 100 using base-10 blocks.
lessons.independent_task: Children represent given numbers to 100 using tens and ones blocks.
key_questions: How many tens and ones make 64?
Can you show me 87?

differentiation.greater_depth: Represent numbers to 100 and compare two numbers

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline check of place value moving into Year 2 — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Practise representing numbers with grouped objects.

lessons.title: Living, Dead, or Never Alive?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sort things into living, dead, and never alive.
success_criteria: I can sort an object correctly.
I can explain my reasoning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the three categories (living, dead, never alive) with examples.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort picture cards into the three categories, recording reasoning.
key_questions: Is this living, dead, or never alive?
How do you know?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for tricky examples (e.g. a fallen leaf, a fossil)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note classification reasoning, an introduction to this term's living things topic — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.plenary: Recap the three categories with examples.
lessons.home_link: Sort 3 objects at home into living/dead/never alive.

lessons.title: Writing About My Summer
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a short recount using past tense consistently.
success_criteria: I can write in the past tense.
I can write 2-3 sentences about my summer.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap past tense verbs (went, saw, played).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a short recount of the summer holiday using consistent past tense.
lessons.independent_task: Children write a short recount of their summer, checking past tense consistency.
key_questions: What did you do this summer?
Is your writing in the past tense throughout?

differentiation.support: Complete sentence frames in past tense
differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ sentences with varied past tense verbs

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline writing assessment for Year 2, focusing on tense consistency — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share recounts with a partner, checking tense.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family about your summer using past tense.

lessons.title: 2D and 3D Shape Properties Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe properties of 2D and 3D shapes.
success_criteria: I can name a 2D and 3D shape.
I can describe a property (sides, faces, edges).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model describing shape properties using correct vocabulary (sides, vertices for 2D; faces, edges, vertices for 3D).
lessons.independent_task: Children sort and describe properties of a range of 2D and 3D shapes.
key_questions: How many sides does this have?
How many faces does this have?

differentiation.greater_depth: Describe less common shapes and compare properties

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline check of shape vocabulary and property knowledge — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Find and describe shapes around your home.

lessons.title: What Do Living Things Need?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe basic needs of living things.
success_criteria: I can name something living things need.
I can say why it's needed.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap what humans need to survive from Year 1.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss basic needs shared by living things (air, water, food, space to live).
lessons.independent_task: Children record what different living things need, comparing a plant, an animal, and a human.
key_questions: What does this living thing need?
Is it the same for all living things?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of shared basic needs of living things — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Talk about what a pet or plant at home needs.

lessons.title: Phonics Baseline: Phase 6 Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to read words with common suffixes and apply Phase 6 spelling patterns.
success_criteria: I can read words with suffixes (-ed, -ing, -er).
I can read at least 5 common exception words.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick-fire flashcard recap of common exception words.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Recap suffixes and model reading words containing them.
lessons.independent_task: Children read a set of levelled words/sentences with suffixes, with the teacher noting fluency for baseline assessment.
key_questions: Can you read this word with the suffix?
Do you know this word by sight?

differentiation.support: Focus on simple suffixed words with 1:1 support
differentiation.greater_depth: Read longer words with multiple suffixes

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline phonics/spelling assessment to group children for the term — evidence for ENG.R1/W1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress and recap key suffixes.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading suffixed words sent home.

lessons.title: Addition and Subtraction to 20 Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to add and subtract within 20 fluently, ready to extend to 100.
success_criteria: I can add within 20.
I can subtract within 20.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Consolidate addition and subtraction to 20 using number lines and known facts.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a range of addition/subtraction problems to 20, checking fluency.
key_questions: Can you solve this without counting from 1?
What strategy did you use?
lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline check before extending to numbers within 100 — evidence for MATHS.N2.

lessons.title: Materials Recap: What Are Things Made Of?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name and describe materials, recapping Year 1 learning.
success_criteria: I can name 5+ materials.
I can describe a property of each.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Consolidate material names and properties (wood, plastic, metal, glass, fabric, rubber).
lessons.independent_task: Children sort and describe properties of a collection of materials.
resources_needed: Collection of objects made from varied materials
key_questions: What material is this?
What property does it have?
lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline consolidation check before this term's materials-changing-shape learning — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Find and name materials of 5 objects at home.

lessons.title: Show and Tell: My Year 2 Goal
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to speak clearly about a personal goal for the year.
success_criteria: I can share a goal for this year.
I can answer one question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what a 'goal' is with examples.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model sharing a personal goal for the year.
lessons.independent_task: Children share a goal for Year 2 with a small group, answering a question.
key_questions: What is your goal for this year?
How will you achieve it?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain how they'll work towards their goal

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline spoken language assessment for Year 2 — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Vote on an inspiring goal shared.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family your goal for Year 2.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Place Value, Shape
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, place value and shape skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can count to 100.
I can represent numbers with tens and ones.
I can describe shape properties.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of counting to 100, place value, and shape properties.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations: counting, place value, shape.
key_questions: What number is this?
What shape is this?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 1 baseline maths assessment for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/GEO.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate a great first week of Year 2 maths.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting to 100 over the weekend.

lessons.title: Science Review: Living Things and Materials
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall living things classification and material properties learned this week.
success_criteria: I can sort living/dead/never alive.
I can name a material and its property.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering living things classification and materials.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet covering the week's science learning.
key_questions: Is this living or never alive?
What material is this?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline science assessment for the term — evidence for SCI.LIV/SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned in science this week with your family.
